rationale: A gives the most balanced presentation: it announces the two regimes, proves the delicate endpoint triple-selection argument in full, and remains more economical than B. B is likewise essentially complete and especially transparent in its claim-by-claim organization, but it is noticeably longer and its hyperplane-transfer paragraph states only the wrong direction of the comparison needed for the ensuing implication, although the displayed formula immediately supplies the missing reverse inequality. D contains the same sound core argument in a useful compressed form, but it cites undefined equations for the pair kernel and point-slice total, leaving more reconstruction to the reader. C does not prove its central dyadic non-endpoint and endpoint lemmas, so most of its substantial detail only transfers an assumed gain to the stated formulation. E is weakest because its “normalized dyadic gain” is essentially the main theorem under normalization and is simply attributed to unspecified earlier work rather than derived from the provided context.
